Body:
## Research findings

Posting notes from a deep-dive into the codebase to inform implementation.

### Provider coverage

**Anthropic direct (`packages/llm` native path)**

The Anthropic API already returns `cache_creation.ephemeral_5m_input_tokens` and `cache_creation.ephemeral_1h_input_tokens` in every `message_start` event — confirmed by live cassette recordings in `packages/llm/test/fixtures/recordings/anthropic-messages-cache/`. Both the nested sub-object and the legacy flat `cache_creation_input_tokens` field (their sum) are present on every response.

The current `AnthropicUsage` Effect Schema in `packages/llm/src/protocols/anthropic-messages.ts` only declares `cache_creation_input_tokens` (the flat total). Effect Schema strips unknown fields during decode, so `cache_creation.ephemeral_5m_input_tokens` and `cache_creation.ephemeral_1h_input_tokens` are **silently dropped today** — they never reach `session.ts`.

**bedrock-converse (`packages/llm` native path)**

AWS Bedrock's Converse API returns a single flat `cacheWriteInputTokens` field in its `metadata` event. There is no per-TTL breakdown in the response — confirmed by the `BedrockUsageSchema` definition and the code comment at `bedrock-converse.ts:423`.

More importantly: tracing the full call chain from `session/llm.ts` → `native-request.ts` → `cache-policy.ts` → `bedrock-cache.ts` reveals that **opencode never sets `ttlSeconds` in the normal execution path**. The `cache` field on `LLMRequest` is never populated by the session runner, so `applyCachePolicy()` resolves to `AUTO` with `ttlSeconds: undefined`. `ttlBucket(undefined)` always returns `undefined`, so `DEFAULT_5M` (`{ cachePoint: { type: "default" } }`) is always emitted. The 1h path (`DEFAULT_1H`) exists and is covered by tests but is only reachable by manually constructing a request with `cache: { ttlSeconds: 3600 }` — no user-facing config exposes this today.

Practical consequence: Bedrock always incurs the 5m write rate (1.25× base). The `cache_write` value in models.dev for Bedrock models is implicitly the 5m rate.

**bedrock-mantle**

This is the OpenAI-compatible endpoint (`bedrock-mantle.<region>.api.aws/openai/v1`) used for OpenAI models hosted on Bedrock (e.g. `openai.gpt-5.5`). It goes through the AI SDK bridge (`packages/opencode/src/session/llm/ai-sdk.ts`), not the native `llm` protocol. It also returns a single `inputTokenDetails.cacheWriteTokens` — no split.

**All other providers**: single `cacheWriteInputTokens` only.

---

### What needs to change

The fix is Anthropic-direct only for the token-level split. The schema and config changes are needed across the board for correctness and custom-provider support:

1. **`packages/llm/src/protocols/anthropic-messages.ts`** — extend `AnthropicUsage` schema to capture `cache_creation.ephemeral_5m_input_tokens` and `cache_creation.ephemeral_1h_input_tokens`; update `mapUsage()` to populate two new fields on `Usage`.

2. **`packages/llm/src/schema/events.ts`** — add `cacheWrite5mInputTokens` and `cacheWrite1hInputTokens` to the `Usage` class; keep `cacheWriteInputTokens` as their sum for backward compatibility.

3. **`packages/core/src/models-dev.ts`** — add `cache_write_5m` / `cache_write_1h` optional fields to `Cost` and `CostTier` schemas.

4. **`packages/opencode/src/provider/provider.ts`** — extend `ProviderCacheCost` with optional `write5m` / `write1h`; update `cost()` mapper and config override block.

5. **`packages/core/src/v1/config/provider.ts`** — add `cache_write_5m` / `cache_write_1h` to the user config cost schema so LiteLLM proxy users and custom-provider users can specify both rates in `opencode.json`.

6. **`packages/opencode/src/session/session.ts`** — extract the split token counts in `getUsage()` and apply separate rates; fall back to `write` for providers that only report a combined total (Bedrock, etc.).

7. **`anomalyco/models.dev`** — upstream schema needs `cache_write_5m` / `cache_write_1h` added to `Cost`; Anthropic-direc

I also explored a small TUI direction for this, based on the Obsidian and shared-mailbox use cases. The permission flow would still be the core of the feature, using the existing `external_directory` behavior described above. Separately, it might be useful to make active or configured external links visible in the UI, so users can tell when a workspace is connected to paths outside the project. One possible treatment would be: * a small footer indicator, such as `↗ 2 Links` * a sidebar `Links` section for a quick overview * an `/status` section showing the link path, resolved target, and relevant permission state Mockups: These are only UI explorations, not a proposal to expand the initial implementation. My preference would be to keep the first change focused on safe consent behavior, then consider TUI visibility as a follow-up if the direction is useful.

Rebased this on the current `dev` branch and moved the filter plumbing to the new v2 API layout.

The old `packages/opencode/.../handlers/v2/session.ts` path is gone upstream now, so the branch now keeps the filter behavior in `SessionV2.list` and exposes `path`, `roots`, and `start` through `packages/server/src/groups/v2/session.ts`.

- `bun test --timeout 30000 test/server/httpapi-session.test.ts -t "honors v2 session list filters"`

+1, experiencing the same issue on Linux.

**Environment:**
- OS: Linux (Fedora)
- OpenCode version: 1.16.2
- Terminal: standard bash terminal

**Symptoms:**

1. **At startup** — before the TUI even renders, a stray sequence appears at the top:
   ```
   ^[[<35;83;40M
   ```

2. **After exit** — the sequence leaks into the shell prompt:
   ```
   user@host:~/projects$ 35;83;40M
   ```

The sequence `35;83;40M` is an SGR mouse report (coordinates 83;40, button 35) that gets echoed after the terminal has already left raw mode. This matches the root cause described in the issue — `setRawMode(false)` re-enabling ECHO before mouse tracking is fully disabled.

The `OPENCODE_DISABLE_MOUSE=true` workaround prevents the issue, but obviously disables mouse support entirely.

Happy to provide any additional debugging info if needed.

Okay, so some more findings: The git bisect here was done with `bun dev --print-logs run "say hello"` and it turns out `bun dev` mode is affected by this in a way that the production build is potentially not. Here's some more AI analysis that feels right to me:

## AI root cause analysis
Near the bottom of the browser build:
```
const no = Symbol.for("node-only");
const parseKnownFiles = no;
```
Every node-only export is deliberately set to Symbol.for("node-only") in the browser CJS build. `@smithy/core@3.24.5` intentionally stubs out filesystem/node-only APIs in its browser condition export as Symbols. When bun dev runs with --conditions=browser, Bun resolves the browser entry in the exports map — which gives `dist-cjs/submodules/config/index.browser.js` — and parseKnownFiles is that Symbol stub.
The parent commit did not have this problem because `@aws-sdk/credential-providers@3.993.0` (the old version) pinned `credential-provider-ini@3.972.29`, which depended on `@smithy/shared-ini-file-loader` and `@smithy/property-provider` directly as separate packages — never routing through `@smithy/core/config`.

The bisect commit bumped `@aws-sdk/credential-providers` to 3.1057.0, which requires `credential-provider-ini@^3.972.46`. That version consolidated its deps into `@smithy/core/config`, a subpath that has a browser stub returning Symbols for all node-only APIs.

So, at the very least, there's a dev dependency with opencode. The next thing for me to figure out is whether there is a separate (possibly) related problem for the production build, or if the homebrew version of opencode (which is what I am using) is misconfigured to use the browser build, rather than what opencode directly provides when building.

Okay, I have put all of the pieces together. There are two related issues going on. I'll leave this issue as open until a maintainer takes a peek, because there's still a problem during development version, even if end users are unaffected since 1.16.2


# Summary
browser-mode bundling is broken for opencode + amazon-bedrock since 1.15.3 due to a fragility in how the code resolution works. This fragility exists today, and any contributor to the codebase running `bun dev` will hit the bug metioned in this issue even today.

For users of distributions, here is the status:
1.15.3 - No bug
1.16.0 - Bug introduced by the changing dependencies
1.16.2 - Bug fixed by switching to [node mode](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/30873) for resolution

Note: Homebrew users are stuck on 1.16.0 until homebrew gets their [PR](https://github.com/Homebrew/homebrew-core/pull/286498) landed


# More details
Fundamentally, the module resolution code of opencode when using `browser` mode is just extremely fragile. Dependencies which pull in other dependencies are liable to cause bundling issues. The bisecting commit [76ee87ead84ab5c5583074a19ea0894c5e8e361a](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/commit/76ee87ead84ab5c5583074a19ea0894c5e8e361a) just happened to cause a new set of dependencies for the amazon bedrock path which triggered this.

This fragility exists today in the main branch, and can easily be reproduced by running `bun dev` when using the amazon-bedrock provider.

Browser mode is going to always cause issues with smithy (and perhaps other modules) for any dependency that explicitly has a split browser version vs node version. The AWS SDK and Smithy packages ship separate browser builds that deliberately stub out every node-only API with Symbol.for("node-only"). When you run a Node.js CLI with --conditions=browser, any package that ships a browser build will silently swap in those stubs. causing this blowup
